source: restates the FEAD/Sigmund 3D cantilever in physical units
brief: Bracket design, rev A Envelope: a rectangular block 200 mm long (x), 100 mm tall (y) and 100 mm deep (z). Steel, E = 210 GPa, nu = 0.3. Mounting: the whole end face at x = 0 is welded to a wall (fully fixed). Load: 1 kN pushing straight down (negative y) on a 10 mm x 10 mm pad in the middle of the free end face (x = 200). Volume fraction 0.3. Mesh at 1 mm elements.
intended: [200, 100, 100] mm; vf 0.3; steel E 210000.0; support wall: face x- fix ['x', 'y', 'z']; load pad: patch x+ c[50, 50] s[10, 10] F [0, -1000, 0]

source: 3D MBB beam (half model), as in Liu & Tovar 2014, top3d
brief: Simply supported beam, symmetric half model The full beam is 240 mm long (x), 40 mm deep (y, up) and 40 mm wide (z), aluminium 6061. It sits on two supports along the bottom edges at its two ends, across the full width; the supports carry vertical and sideways load only. A 2 kN downward line load acts across the full width at mid-span on the top surface. Model only the left half (x from 0 to 120 mm) and use symmetry at mid-span. Volume fraction 0.3, 1 mm elements.
intended: [120, 40, 40] mm; vf 0.3; aluminium 6061 E 69000.0; support end_support: edge along z at [0, 0] fix ['y', 'z']; support symmetry: face x+ fix ['x']; load midspan: edge along z at [120, 40] F [0, -1000, 0]
admissible: full 240 mm model with both end supports and the full 2 kN | the end support also fixes x (pinned)
notes: Half of the 2 kN acts on the half model.

source: FEAD bridge with a distributed deck load
brief: Bridge segment A deck segment spanning 400 mm (x), 100 mm high (y, up) and 100 mm wide (z), steel. It rests on two bearings along the bottom edges at each end, running across the full width. The left bearing is pinned; the right one lets the deck expand along the span. A uniform 5 kN load acts downward on the entire top surface. Volume fraction 0.25, 2 mm elements.
intended: [400, 100, 100] mm; vf 0.25; steel E 210000.0; support pin: edge along z at [0, 0] fix ['x', 'y', 'z']; support expansion: edge along z at [400, 0] fix ['y', 'z']; load deck: face y+ F [0, -5000, 0]
admissible: Right roller fixes y only; x and z free, left pinned edge unchanged.

brief: Shaft bracket in torsion Envelope 160 mm long (x) with an 80 x 80 mm square cross-section (y up, z), steel. The x = 0 end is bolted rigidly to a gearbox. At the far end (x = 160) a 40 N*m torque about +x (right-hand rule) is applied through two 16 x 16 mm drive lugs on the end face: one flush with the top edge (y = 80), one flush with the bottom edge (y = 0), both centred at z = 40. Each lug carries an equal and opposite force along z. Volume fraction 0.3, 2 mm elements.
intended: [160, 80, 80] mm; vf 0.3; steel E 210000.0; support gearbox: face x- fix ['x', 'y', 'z']; load lug_top: patch x+ c[72, 40] s[16, 16] F [0, 0, 625]; load lug_bottom: patch x+ c[8, 40] s[16, 16] F [0, 0, -625]
notes: 40 N*m = 40000 N*mm; the lug centres are 64 mm apart, so a 625 N couple in z. M_x = r_y F_z: the top lug (r_y = +32) pushes +z.

source: 3D L-bracket benchmark (e.g. Le et al. 2010), keep-out as a passive void
brief: L-bracket Envelope 100 x 100 x 40 mm (x, y, z), y up, steel. The upper-right corner region, x > 40 mm and y > 40 mm, is occupied by another part and must stay empty through the full depth. The top face of the vertical arm (y = 100, x from 0 to 40) is bolted to the ceiling. A 500 N downward load acts on a 10 x 10 mm pad on the right end face of the horizontal arm (x = 100), centred at y = 20 and mid-depth. Volume fraction 0.3, 1 mm elements.
intended: [100, 100, 40] mm; vf 0.3; steel E 210000.0; support ceiling: patch y+ c[20, 20] s[40, 40] fix ['x', 'y', 'z']; load tip: patch x+ c[20, 20] s[10, 10] F [0, -500, 0]; void occupied: box [40, 40, 0]–[100, 100, 40]

brief: Motor mount Plate envelope 160 x 60 x 120 mm (x, y, z), y up, aluminium 6061. It bolts to the machine bed through four M10 bolts on its bottom face (y = 0) at x = 20 and 140 mm, z = 20 and 100 mm; each bolt clamps through a 24 mm washer. Keep a solid boss of 24 mm diameter and 10 mm height around each bolt. The motor sits on a 40 x 40 mm, 5 mm thick solid pad on the top face, centred at x = 80, z = 60. Its mounting pad carries 2 kN downward and 0.8 kN sideways (+x) from belt tension. Volume fraction 0.2, 1 mm elements.
intended: [160, 60, 120] mm; vf 0.2; aluminium 6061 E 69000.0; support bolt_1: patch y- c[20, 20] s[24, 24] fix ['x', 'y', 'z']; support bolt_2: patch y- c[20, 100] s[24, 24] fix ['x', 'y', 'z']; support bolt_3: patch y- c[140, 20] s[24, 24] fix ['x', 'y', 'z']; support bolt_4: patch y- c[140, 100] s[24, 24] fix ['x', 'y', 'z']; load motor: patch y+ c[80, 60] s[40, 40] F [800, -2000, 0]; solid boss_1: cylinder y c[20, 20] r12; solid boss_2: cylinder y c[20, 100] r12; solid boss_3: cylinder y c[140, 20] r12; solid boss_4: cylinder y c[140, 100] r12; solid pad: box [60, 55, 40]–[100, 60, 80]
notes: Bolt holes inside the bosses are not modelled: the bolt fills the hole, and a keep-out hole inside a keep-in boss would conflict (R007).

brief: Sensor arm Envelope 150 x 30 x 30 mm, the arm running along x. It carries a 2 kg camera (about 20 N) at the far end, mounted on a 20 x 20 mm plate in the middle of the end face at x = 150 mm. The arm attaches to the robot frame. Steel, volume fraction 0.25, 1 mm elements.
intended: [150, 30, 30] mm; vf 0.25; steel E 210000.0; support frame: face x- fix ['x', 'y', 'z']; load camera: patch x+ c[15, 15] s[20, 20] F [0, -20, 0]
oracle: where and how the arm attaches: The x = 0 end face is bolted flat to the frame; treat it as fully fixed. | direction of the camera load: Gravity acts along -y.
admissible: 20 x 20 x 2 mm retained camera plate at x=148..150, with oracle root and -y load.
notes: Two decision-relevant gaps: the attachment and the load direction.

brief: Slider bracket Envelope 120 x 40 x 40 mm (x, y, z), y up, steel. It rides on a linear rail along its whole bottom face (y = 0): the rail holds it vertically and sideways but lets it slide freely along x. A 300 N push along +x acts on a 10 x 10 mm pad at the centre of the left end face (x = 0). Volume fraction 0.3, 1 mm elements.
intended: [120, 40, 40] mm; vf 0.3; steel E 210000.0; support rail: face y- fix ['y', 'z']; load push: patch x- c[20, 20] s[10, 10] F [300, 0, 0]
oracle: any other support or an end stop: No, it is supported only by the rail.
notes: As stated the part is a mechanism along x (rule R003): nothing reacts the push. A correct agent reports that and asks for an x restraint rather than inventing one.

brief: Pedestrian bridge model with cable duct Span 300 mm (x), 60 mm high (y, up), 60 mm wide (z), steel. Both bottom end edges rest on bearings across the full width: left pinned, right free to slide along the span. 3 kN acts downward on the full top surface. A 16 mm diameter cable duct runs across the full width (along z) at x = 150 mm, y = 20 mm and must stay empty. No member may be thinner than 3 mm. Volume fraction 0.25, 1 mm elements.
intended: [300, 60, 60] mm; vf 0.25; steel E 210000.0; support pin: edge along z at [0, 0] fix ['x', 'y', 'z']; support slide: edge along z at [300, 0] fix ['y', 'z']; load deck: face y+ F [0, -3000, 0]; void duct: cylinder z c[150, 20] r8
admissible: Right bearing fixes y only; x and z free; retain left pin, duct and 3 mm minimum. | Right bearing fixes y only; x and z free; duct and feature size unchanged.

brief: Hook plate Plate envelope 120 x 80 x 20 mm (x, y, z), y up, steel. It is bolted along its top face (y = 80) to a beam. A 1.5 kN load hangs from the lower corner. Volume fraction 0.3, 1 mm elements.

source: 3D torsion benchmark family (Michell-type torsion in a box domain)
brief: Block in torsion A 100 mm cube (x, y, z), z up, steel. The bottom face (z = 0) is bolted down over its full area. An 18 N*m torque about +z (right-hand rule, counter-clockwise seen from above) is applied to the top face through four 10 x 10 mm pads, one at the midpoint of each top edge and flush with that edge. Each pad carries an equal force tangential to the edge it sits on. Volume fraction 0.15, 1 mm elements.
intended: [100, 100, 100] mm; vf 0.15; steel E 210000.0; support base: face z- fix ['x', 'y', 'z']; load pad_front: patch z+ c[50, 5] s[10, 10] F [100, 0, 0]; load pad_right: patch z+ c[95, 50] s[10, 10] F [0, 100, 0]; load pad_back: patch z+ c[50, 95] s[10, 10] F [-100, 0, 0]; load pad_left: patch z+ c[5, 50] s[10, 10] F [0, -100, 0]
notes: Pad centres are 45 mm from the axis: 4 x 45 mm x F = 18000 N*mm gives F = 100 N. M_z = r_x F_y - r_y F_x.
